Hi Marcus / Maya,

Great news — Sophia (ex-Scale/Meta researcher) has indicated strong interest but has a competing counteroffer with a headline base + equity refresh. I attached the draft offer (base + stock + typical sign-on). Recruiting recommends an exception here: candidate brings production inference + quantization expertise we don’t see often, and she has active engagements with a major prospect (Neudata) that would materially speed our integrations backlog.

Requested uplift proposal from candidate side:
- Base: $215k (we currently cap band ~$190k for Sr LLM Eng)

- Equity: +0.15% one-time refresh on top of standard grant (to be vested on 2 years)

Can you and compensation review and approve an out-of-band package? Recruiting needs a yes/no to lock candidate this week.

Ben

Team,

Putting this in front of comp & people — candidate looks exceptionally strong on inference optimizations and productization (KV cache, batching, runtime ops). She also has contacts at Neudata which could accelerate our platform integrations; recruiting flagged that as incremental commercial value.

My ask: approve an exception for the one-time items and a modest base uplift to land the offer in a competitive range. Specific ask to approve:
- Base to $210k (mid-band + ~10%)
- One-time sign-on $30k
- Equity refresh +0.15% one-time grant

Rationale: we avoid losing to counteroffer and preserve long-term cost via a small equity refresh instead of materially raising comp band. If we need to cap, prioritize sign-on + equity and keep base at band ceiling ($195k).

Timing: Recruiting would like final sign-off by EOD 11/17 PST so they can present Monday. I’ve attached our comp_band_vs_market spreadsheet for quick reference.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Director, Talent & Hiring Ops
Redwood Inference

Marcus / Maya —

Thanks for the context. I pulled comp data and flagged the following:
- Benchmark for Sr LLM Eng (West coast) median base ~190–195k; top 75th is ~205–215k depending on public comps.
- We have limited precedence for >0.1% one-time refresh for this level, but folks with strong product + sales motion upside have received one-time refreshes tied to commercial outcomes.

Proposal from People/Comp:
- Approve one-time sign-on: $30,000 (lump sum)
- Approve equity refresh: +0.12% one-time, contingent on 6-month milestone tied to Neudata introduction or platform delivery (simple OKR)
- Base: approve up to $200,000 (band ceiling + small stretch). If hiring manager insists on >$200k, we need exec approval and to document commercial upside.

If we agree to the contingency for the refresh, we can limit longer-term cost while still making the package compelling. Laura, please confirm if payroll/tax/legal sees any issues with the sign-on structure.

Grace O'Connor
Head of People Ops
Redwood Inference

Agree with Grace's conservative path. Quick notes from HR/legal review:
- One-time sign-on $30k as a taxable lump sum is fine; will run through payroll with normal withholdings.
- One-time equity refresh +0.12% is permissible but must be structured as a separate grant with explicit vesting conditions (we usually do 50% at 6 months / 50% at 12 months for refresh grants tied to milestones).
- If we attach a commercial milestone tied to Neudata introductions, we need the hiring manager to define a measurable acceptance criteria (Doc/Intro/PO).

Final approval (People + HR) — Approve the following package to present to candidate:
- Base: $200,000
- One-time sign-on: $30,000
- One-time equity refresh: +0.12% (milestone: documented Neudata intro or first paid pilot within 9 months; vesting 50% at 6 months, 50% at 12 months)

Marcus — if you and Maya approve, recruiting can send the offer as final. Please copy People when you send.

Laura Bennett
VP, People Operations
Redwood Inference
